pr_title: add some more examples for release create

issue_context.title: gh create release does not respect the flags, always prompts for user input
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

```
gh --version
gh version 1.9.1 (2021-04-15)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v1.9.1
```

Problem: gh prompts for a title, draft, pre-release even when  provided via command line. Also these are optional. 
* It seems that the `[FLAGS]` is not respected


### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Here is a repro example:
1) Run `gh release create` as shown below:
```
$ gh -R <my-repo> release create --draft --title "New Draft"   v1.7 darwin-amd64-v1.7.zip
? Title (optional) New Draft
? Release notes Leave blank
? Is this a prerelease? No
? Submit? Publish release
https://github.com/<my-repo>/releases/tag/v1.7
```

### Expected vs actual behavior

* Actual: gh prompts user for title, release notes, pre-release etc

* Expected: gh to create a release without prompt

### Logs

I do not see [FLAGS] in usage.

```
gh release create --help
....

USAGE
  gh release create <tag> [<files>...]

FLAGS
  -d, --draft             Save the release as a draft instead of publishing it
  -n, --notes string      Release notes
  -F, --notes-file file   Read release notes from file
  -p, --prerelease        Mark the release as a prerelease
      --target branch     Target branch or full commit SHA (default: main branch)
  -t, --title string      Release title

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format
```
comments:
Hi, thanks for writing in! This is actually designed behavior. The `--title` attribute is optional in GitHub Releases, so supplying it doesn't turn off interactive mode. It's the `--notes` attribute that needs to be supplied in order to use this command in scripts. For a release with blank notes, use `--notes ""`.

We should do a better job at pointing this out in documentation. I will re-label this issue as a docs ticket.

Ref. #2632
